threads.body: [General] An empty `IncludeExclude` carries no configuration, but this path treats it as active. Because an empty selector's `matches()` method matches every value, calling either new builder setter with `IncludeExclude.builder().build()` captures all request metadata instead of capturing nothing. Normalize empty selectors to the absent state here.

replies.body:
Addressed in d95871d90771c95cb78a9e00b2b52c497eea06c1.

Analysis: Programmatic builder callers can pass an empty selector directly, bypassing the declarative configuration normalization. Treating null and empty selectors identically in the extractor constructor prevents the empty selector's match-all behavior from capturing metadata.

Upsides: Empty selectors consistently capture nothing across declarative and programmatic configuration, and the focused regression test covers a valid metadata key.

Downsides: Adds one inexpensive isEmpty() check when constructing the extractor.

threads.body: [General] This no-argument lookup reads the globally initialized preview flag instead of the configuration carried by the `openTelemetry` argument. If that instance enables `java.common.v3_preview`, deprecated `capture_metadata` aliases can remain active. Resolve preview mode from the same instance, as the other configuration readers do.

replies.body:
Addressed in 80542a332b869aeacce9c7ad92448e63284d7074.

Analysis: The no-argument preview accessor is initialized from GlobalOpenTelemetry and can disagree with the OpenTelemetry instance passed to GrpcConfig.create(). Resolving preview mode with that instance keeps the gRPC configuration tree and common preview flag in the same configuration context.

Upsides: Deprecated metadata aliases are reliably disabled for instance-scoped v3 preview configuration, including library users that do not configure GlobalOpenTelemetry.

Downsides: No material downside identified.
